messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Sudden spike in /v1/embeddings write path from APAC edge (eu/apac egress) — 6x median QPS and rising. Elevated 5xx and 429s. Investigate and mitigate.
Alice Chen: I see it. Latency for embeddings up ~300ms p90 -> p95 and error rate to 5%. Starting triage.
Marco Li: Can you post top offending IP prefixes / keys? I'll look for header patterns.
Sara G: Quick check: many requests are short seq_len=16, high concurrency per API key, rotating UA strings. Smells like scraper farm using stolen keys.
Ryan (ProdEng): Suggest temporary soft-limit per-key enforcement and enforce per-ip bucket at edge. We can also flip on stricter KV cache TTL to reduce backend load.
Alice Chen: Agreed. Marco, can you push an edge-rate rule to cap embeddings to 6rps per key with a 10s sliding window as soft-limit and 1rps hard? Do we have a safe rollout config?
Marco Li: Pushing a rule to edge now. Config snippet:
```
route: /v1/embeddings
match: region == "apac" && kind == "embed"
actions:
  - type: rate_limit
    per: api_key
    soft_rps: 6
    hard_rps: 1
    penalty: 10s
```
Marco Li: Applied to edge canaries (apac-1) — monitoring; will scale to apac-2 in 2m if stable.
incident-bot: Deploy log: edge-rule-apac-embed-rate applied to apac-1 at 5223456990 by Marco Li
Sara G: We've also added a header-fingerprint filter for obvious churners (same Accept-Language, rotating UA). Sending rule to WAF tag group B.
security-bot: WAF: added signature 0xA7 for rotating-ua-embed-scraper; action=block if matches > 3 reqs/10s from same fingerprint.
Ryan (ProdEng): Recommend disabling async batch endpoint for new unverified keys to reduce amplification. That will break a small percentage of legit partners — CC CS and Support.
Emily (Support): Already seeing ~8 support tickets citing 429s on embeddings. If we disable batching for unverified keys, please prepare customer message draft.
Amanda (CS): Draft: "We're seeing an abusive traffic pattern affecting embeddings in APAC. We're applying protective rate limits and may temporarily restrict batch endpoints for unverified keys. Expect transient 429s. We're working to restore normal service." Approve?
Alice Chen: Approve. Post to status and prepare targeted emails for 3 customers hitting >1000 reqs/min.
Marco Li: Added proactive geo-blackhole for two suspicious prefixes (apac ranges). Monitoring — traffic dropped ~45% to backend.
Sara G: Backend CPU dropped 30% after edge rules and geo block. Error rate down to 1.2% now. Good signal.
incident-bot: paging: handing off to next oncall Marco Li at 5223457800
Marco Li: Taking over. Next steps: continue canary to full rollout if error rate stays <2% and latency p95 < 250ms for 10m.
Ryan (ProdEng): Follow-up: we'll enable KV cache short-circuit for frequent small embeds to bypass some compute paths. Patch coming in 15m.
Emily (Support): Sent status update to status.redwood.ai: "Performance degradation in APAC embeddings mitigated; applying rate limits and WAF rules. Minimal customer impact expected." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/5223456789
Amanda (CS): Reached out to the 3 high-volume customers. One confirmed suspicious activity and will rotate keys. Two asked for ETA — told them 1-2 hours for full remediation.
Sara G: Final check: no rollout regressions, error rate steady at 0.9%, p95 latency 190ms. Recommend leave rules in place for 4 hours then reassess.
Alice Chen: Agree. I'll set a reminder to review in 4 hours and coordinate key revocations for affected customers if needed.
Marco Li: Closing active mitigation phase. If anything flares, call the channel or page oncall. Thanks team :heart:
